title: Model telemetry signature and pinned-release manifest for onboarding artifacts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and deliver a canonical telemetry signature artifact and a pinned-release manifest to be published with every verified model onboarding. The goal is to provide a compact, verifiable fingerprint and release contract that runtime, Console, and Dedicated can consume for deterministic routing, rollback, and canarying without re-running large-scale benchmarks. This ticket covers schema decisions, signing/rotation policy, storage & discoverability, and automation hooks for publish/refresh.
acceptance_criteria: A stable telemetry signature format (human-readable + compact hash) is specified and documented in the onboarding playbook.

Pinned-release manifest schema defined with fields: model_name, model_version, runtime_compatibility, canonical_latency_samples_uri, normalized_cost_estimate, kv_cache_behavior_hint, quantization_profile_id, signature_hash, signed_by, signed_at, and canary_policy.
Automated signer service and key rotation flow documented and implemented in the publish CI job (integration test verifies signature verification).
Console and Dedicated control plane can fetch manifest and validate signature to enforce pinned-version routing and safe rollback decisions.
Backward compatibility test: older runtimes gracefully ignore optional fields and reject manifests with unsupported runtime_compatibility ranges.
Publish job attaches links to canonical telemetry samples (s3:// or gs://) and a lightweight summary CSV for quick cost/latency checks in Console.
Security review completed for storage and signing flow; audit log entries emitted on publish and rotation events.
implementation_steps: Draft manifest schema and example manifests and circulate to Runtime, Console, and Eng-Infra for feedback
Prototype signature generation in onboarding CI using ephemeral KMS key; run end-to-end verification step
Add manifest generation to onboarding pipeline: collect sampled latency histogram, cost estimate, and KV-cache hint
Integrate manifest fetch+validation into Console UI: show signed-by, last-signed, and compatibility score
Add runtime hooks: on model load, verify manifest signature and enforce pinned-version table for routing
Create canary policy runner that reads canary_policy and schedules shadowing experiments per manifest
Run cross-team integration test against Dedicated staging and iterate on schema fields
Finalize docs and run security review checklist; publish playbook update.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: embed full latency histogram vs. publish a URI to bucket with signed index. Chosen: keep manifest light (summary + URI) to avoid large payloads and reduce signing surface.
Decision: use SHA256(base64) of canonicalized manifest JSON as signature target. Use KMS-backed signer and rotate keys quarterly.
Fallback semantics: if manifest verification fails at runtime, fall back to model variant mapping in routing table and emit critical alert.
